newsitem.title: USA: Rains soak eastern Corn Belt, seen slowing harvest.
newsitem.headline: Rains soak eastern Corn Belt, seen slowing harvest.

text.p: Rains soaked much of the eastern Corn Belt during the last 24 hours and could keep farmers out of the fields in some areas for two to three days, meteorologists said Friday.

Joel Burgio, agricultural meteorologist with Weather Services Corp, said 0.50 to 2.50 inches fell in southeast Missouri, southern and east-central Illinois, most of Indiana (except the northwest corner), Michigan, Ohio and Kentucky.
He noted the heaviest rainfall of 2.00 to 2.50 inches was seen in central/southern Indiana into Kentucky. In the western Corn Belt there were, however, just a "couple of sprinkles."
"In Minnesota, Iowa, northwest Illinois and even northern Missouri prospects for harvesting are pretty good," he said.
Burgio said there might be some snow flurries Friday in eastern Minnesota, northeast Iowa, northern Illinois, much of Indiana, much of Ohio, Michigan and Wisconsin.
There should not cause serious harvest delays but could "slow down the drying process," he said.
Otherwise, there was not much additional precipitation in the forecast for the Corn Belt through the middle of next week, WSC's Burgio said.

"The rains are done across the Midwest and no major precip events are expected during the next week. This weekend, the vast majority of the belt will be dry," Jon Davis, of Smith Barney, wrote in his daily weather outlook.
Davis said 10 to 15 percent of the belt, made up of northern Ohio, southern Michigan and parts of northern Indiana, would get rain and snow showers this week.
"Thus, 85 to 90 percent of the Midwest will be dry.The relatively dry pattern during the next week will favor late harvest activity as fieldwork conditions gradually improve," Davis added.
